archetype.name: Playoff Team (goalie-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose winning record rests on elite goaltending and a stingy shot wall in front of it. Its puck possession, power play and depth scoring are all middling to poor, so the margin for error is thin when the starter sits.

report.headline: Ullmark is carrying a thin-shooting team; the record outruns the margin
report.take:
Ottawa is 8-4-0, third in the Atlantic and 12th on the site, but the standings flatter a team with a +4 goal differential that ranks 13th per game. What it does well is clear. It keeps shots away, allowing only 23.3 a game (5th), and it has a goalie playing out of his mind. Linus Ullmark is at .945 with 8.4 GSAx across 8 starts, second on the goalie tab. That pairing explains a defense ranked 8th in goals against and a 2.83 allowed-per-game mark well under the league's 3.15.

The split between the two goalies is the real story. In Samuel Ersson's 3 starts he has posted an .835 save percentage and -5.7 GSAx, which drags the team's Goalies GSAx to a pedestrian 0.5 (18th). The ugly losses, 2-7 to St. Louis and 2-6 to San Jose, sit right next to tight wins. This is a team that wins when Ullmark is in net and gets blown out often enough otherwise. Last season's history shows how much this matters: the team's goalies were at -24 GSAx with a 99-point finish despite a strong 55.6% xGF. This year the goaltending has flipped and the underlying play has slipped.

What the record hides is an offense that doesn't generate much. Ottawa takes 25.4 shots a game (27th) and ranks 23rd in CF % at 47%, meaning opponents usually have the puck at 5-on-5. The power play is converting 11.5%, 29th and nearly ten points under the league average. Scoring is level with the league only because the forwards are finishing well and Tim Stützle is playing at a top-five center level, with 16 points. A 5-on-5 PDO of 103 and a +1.3 Pts vs Goal Diff (7th) say some of the 8-4 is bounces and close-game luck. Both overtime wins came in 3-2 and 2-1 games. Over the last 10 the team scored 31 and allowed 31.

The direction depends on two things. One is how many games Ullmark can start at this level. The other is whether a power play that ran at 24% last season comes back. The xGF % of 52.1% says Ottawa still wins the chance battle when it matters, so this isn't a mirage. But it is more of a 95-to-100-point team than the 109-point pace suggests.

strengths.title: Ullmark playing at an elite level
strengths.body: Ullmark's .945 save percentage and 8.4 GSAx in 8 starts make him the second-ranked goalie on the site and the main reason Ottawa allows under three goals a game. No goalie holds .945 over a season, so expect regression. Even a good-not-great Ullmark would still be a big upgrade on last year's crease.

strengths.title: Few shots allowed
strengths.body: Ottawa allows just 23.3 shots a game, 5th in the league and 3.6 under average, with a B+ blueline doing its part. That is structural rather than lucky. It holds up even when possession tilts the other way, and it should travel.

strengths.title: Stützle-Batherson top line
strengths.body: Stützle (16 points, 59.2% xGF, 5th among centers) and Batherson (12 points, 10th among right wings) drive the offense. Giroux and Zetterlund post strong xGF numbers in support. The top of the lineup is legitimately good. The question is what sits beneath it.

concerns.title: Power play has stalled
concerns.body: At 11.5%, Ottawa's power play ranks 29th and sits nearly ten points under the league average. That is a sharp drop from the 24% it ran last season with a similar core. Twelve games is a small sample and the history suggests a rebound, but for now it is costing the team goals in an offense that already struggles to get shots.

concerns.title: Low volume, losing possession
concerns.body: Ottawa ranks 27th in shots a game and 23rd in CF %, a step back from last year's 53%. It is scoring at a league-average rate only because of good finishing and a 103 PDO, which tends to drift back toward 100. If the shooting cools, goals get scarce.

concerns.title: Backup crease is a liability
concerns.body: Ersson's .835 save percentage and -5.7 GSAx in 3 starts put him 68th of 69 goalies. That cancels most of Ullmark's work at the team level. Every night Ullmark sits is a coin flip at best, which matters on back-to-backs.

trend.note: Ottawa has never lost two straight, but it has alternated tidy wins with lopsided losses. The last 10 games came out dead even on goals, with 31 scored and 31 allowed, below the season's +4 overall margin.

weekAhead.headline: Four-game western road trip, three against bottom-half teams
weekAhead.body:
The trip opens in Vegas against a peer: the 11th-ranked Golden Knights, with A-grade forwards and 29.8 shots a game. They also carry D+ goaltending and a 67.7% penalty kill. After that come three teams ranked 21st or worse on the site. Los Angeles is 2-5-2, 30th, with an F blueline. Anaheim is 25th and gives up the third-most winger production relative to expectation. San Jose is the trap, having already beaten Ottawa 6-2, with A- goaltending and a 6.3 Goalies GSAx that keeps a team losing the shot battle afloat.

The schedule hands Ottawa's slumping power play its best chance yet. Vegas and Los Angeles both rank 28th or worse on the penalty kill. The Halloween and November 1 back-to-back in San Jose and Anaheim almost certainly means Ersson starts once, so how Ullmark's starts are split matters. Three of four points-wise is a fair bar.

keyMatchups.title: Power play vs. leaky kills
keyMatchups.body: Vegas kills 67.7% and Los Angeles 65.5%, 28th and 31st. If Ottawa's 29th-ranked power play can't cash in against these two kills, the problem is more than early-season noise.

keyMatchups.title: Vegas forwards test the shot wall
keyMatchups.body: Vegas generates 29.8 shots a game with an A forward group and a 54.6% xGF. That is the stiffest test this week of Ottawa's league-best-tier shot suppression. Vegas's D+ goaltending gives Ottawa's top line room to win a track meet if it comes to that.

keyMatchups.title: San Jose's hot goaltending
keyMatchups.body: The Sharks get outshot (30.1 against a game) and sit 29th in xGF %, but their goalies are 4th in GSAx and their power play converts 26.8%. Ottawa's low shot volume is exactly the profile a hot goalie can frustrate.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts the Halloween/Nov. 1 back-to-back, and whether Ersson can give Ottawa a competitive game.

restOfSeason.body:
The 109-point pace won't hold. Ullmark at .945 will regress, the 5-on-5 PDO of 103 will drift down, and close-game luck rarely stays at +1.3. Two things are sustainable and give this team a real floor: the shot suppression and a positive xGF %. The power play also has room to climb back toward the 23-24% of the last two seasons. Expect goals allowed to creep toward the league average and scoring to hold roughly steady as the power play offsets cooler finishing.

That profile lands Ottawa in the mid-90s to around 100 points, in the playoff mix in a crowded Atlantic rather than at its top. The biggest swing is the crease. A healthy, above-average Ullmark starting most of the remaining 70 games makes this a playoff team. Ersson getting a big share of starts at his current level would push it back to the bubble.
swingFactors: Depth scoring behind Stützle and Batherson

confidence.note: Only 12 games, with results swinging on which goalie starts.
